analysis.title: 11/6 Mkt Internal Wkly: 3 Capitulation Signals vs. 3 Systematic unwinds: Expect a monday low
key_insights: Three capitulation signals have triggered: Excess Flow of -$365bn (largest on record), UBS RMM Flow bought the dip at the 68%-tile vs. 3Y after 1.25 days of selling that was the largest selling episode since Covid, and VIX Cross-Asset Rank at 96%.

The desk reads the three signals as pointing to significant forced selling and oversold conditions, and expects SPX could set a low on Monday as systematic selling and hedge-fund unwind pressure fade.
Three systematic strategies sold an estimated $170-210bn in aggregate on the day: Risk Control $95-125bn, Leveraged ETFs $50-55bn, and CTA $25-30bn.

Risk Control could sell another $200-270bn over the next two days, about $100-135bn per day. After Monday, Risk Control and CTA sell-rebalancing flows are expected to become very small, which reduces their market impact.
UBS PB L/S Net Leverage is at the 18%-tile vs 1Y and the L/S Ratio is at the 8%-tile vs 1Y, so net long exposure is already very low and short-squeeze risk is elevated.

Client conversations on the day were not panicked. Investors expect more systematic selling and are waiting for entry points to buy the dip, which the desk reads as interest in deploying capital into weakness rather than broad capitulation.
risk_factors: Additional systematic selling is still ahead, with Risk Control estimated at $100-135bn per day over the next two days.
The expected Monday low depends on Risk Control and CTA selling fading after Monday.
vol_and_positioning: VIX Cross-Asset Rank at 96%, meaning equity volatility is very elevated relative to nearly every other asset class.
UBS PB L/S Net Leverage at 18%-tile vs 1Y and L/S Ratio at 8%-tile vs 1Y: net long exposure is low and short-squeeze risk is elevated.
Estimated systematic selling on the day of $170-210bn: Risk Control $95-125bn, Leveraged ETFs $50-55bn, CTA $25-30bn. Risk Control may sell a further $200-270bn over the next two days.
Excess Flow of -$365bn is the largest on record.
